GROUNDING (plan-review E4/G6): empirical spike of pydantic-ai 1.107.x exhaustion cause chain, run in-environment against the real PydanticAIRunner over an offline FunctionModel (ALLOW_MODEL_REQUESTS off).

Case A - VALIDATION exhaustion (model returns unparseable text every turn): the terminating exception chain is
  UnretryableOutputError(current S2 translation) -> UnexpectedModelBehavior('Exceeded maximum output retries') -> ToolRetryError -> ModelRetry -> StructuredOutputError(ORIGINAL Rebar object).
The identical original StructuredOutputError IS reachable on the standard __cause__/__context__ chain because S2's pai_output.output_function raises ModelRetry(str(err)) from err (confirmed in source; concision_guard likewise for the transient finish_reason=error branch). So S3 walks the chain and re-raises that exact object, preserving subtype.

Case B - TRUNCATION/concision exhaustion (finish_reason=length every turn): the chain is
  UnretryableOutputError -> UnexpectedModelBehavior -> ModelRetry(CONCISION_INSTRUCTION, BARE).
No Rebar object is present below the ModelRetry, because concision_guard raises ModelRetry(CONCISION_INSTRUCTION) WITHOUT from err. So the cause-chain walk finds nothing -> S3 falls back to constructing a fresh UnretryableOutputError.

Consequence for the plan: AC2 respecified - validation exhaustion re-raises the IDENTICAL StructuredOutputError; repeated-truncation exhaustion surfaces a freshly-constructed UnretryableOutputError (the defined chain-absent fallback). Both pinned by tests (identity via id(); fallback via type+absence).
